postTitle: Shared Households: Money for Three or More Adults
topic: When one flatmate leaves and the room stays empty, the rest carry the rent

assumptions.notes: Four adults, net monthly incomes €5,000, €3,000, €2,000 and €1,000, total €11,000. Shared costs €3,200 a month (€2,400 rent, €300 utilities, €500 food), 29% of income. Split by income, Alma pays €1,455. If Alma leaves and her room stays empty: income left €6,000; rent and utilities stay at €2,700; food falls by about a quarter to €375; new total €3,075, 51% of €6,000. The household saves €125 on food and has to find €1,455 minus €125 = €1,330 a month while the room is empty. Illustrative.

beats.narration: Then Alma leaves and her room stays empty. Rent and utilities stay. Food falls a quarter. Costs hit fifty one percent of income.
The three who stay save a little on food, but have to find one thousand three hundred and thirty euros a month.
This is the exit test. For each person, ask what the household would cost the rest if they left next month.

caption.instagram:
Four flatmates: the bills take 29% of income. One moves out: 51%.

Four adults share €3,200 of costs a month, split by income. Alma, the top earner, pays €1,455. If she leaves and her room stays empty, rent and utilities stay at €2,700 and food falls to about €375: €3,075 on €6,000 of income. The three who stay save €125 on food and have to find €1,330 a month until someone new moves in. In many places a shared lease makes each tenant liable for the whole rent, so the gap is theirs either way.

The exit test, for each person: what they pay now, what would fall if they left, the monthly gap, and how many months the shared buffer covers it.
